newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu aide says Arafat uses "big lie" tactic.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu aide says Arafat uses "big lie" tactic.

text.p: A senior aide to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accused Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Thursday of using a "big lie" to pressure Israel during talks on a long-delayed Israeli troop pullback from Hebron.
"What especially worries me is his (Arafat's) use of what can only be called 'the big lie'," Netanyahu's communications adviser David Bar-Illan told Army radio.
"(Arafat) used 'the big lie' yesterday when he spoke about apartheid, colonialism and racism...it seems this is all a last minute tactic," Bar-Illan said.
Arafat said in Cairo on Wednesday he was enraged by an Israeli troop redeployment proposal.
"It's a dangerous operation. It shows Israel's aggressive intentions in Hebron and shows complete and abhorrent racism," Arafat told reporters.
Arafat said the plan would, among other things, divide the West Bank town in two and give Israel the right to pursue Arabs anywhere it wanted in Hebron, including in Palestinian-ruled areas.
Bar-Illan rejected Arafat's comments and said Israel merely sought security guarantees for 400 Jewish settlers living in armed compounds amidst 100,000 Palestinians in Hebron.
"If he (Arafat) truly thinks that...he will achieve greater American pressure after the (U.S.) elections, he is mistaken," Bar-Illan said.
Israeli and Palestinian negotiators were to resume U.S.-brokered talks in Egypt's Red Sea resort of Taba at 0900 GMT on Thursday.
The Hebron pullback, agreed to by Israel's previous government, was due to have been implemented in March but was delayed after Moslem suicide bombings killed scores in Israel.
Netanyahu seeks modifications in the Hebron deal to safeguard the Jewish settlers in the heart of the city. Palestinians reject any changes in the signed accord.
